clue.text: To sports grounds I went for spicy food

indicators.note: the letter I has gone away, leaving the word for sports grounds without it

parts.note: stadia is a plural of stadium, a sports ground
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to the stadiums in search of something hot to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I went' tells you the letter I leaves the plural of stadium. A tostada is a crisp fried Mexican tortilla with toppings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a toasted Mexican tortilla, often served with chilli toppings, so a piquant dish.

clue.text: Modified views, struggling mid-term

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A government halfway through its term has to shift its opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: To trim is to adjust one's opinions to suit the times, as a political trimmer does; the anagram of MID-TERM gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who trims adjusts opinions to the prevailing wind, so the verb covers altered positions.

clue.text: Coppers making very little difference

definitions.meaning: a trivial amount, an insignificant sum

explanation.definitionFit: Loose coins of low value, and figuratively something of negligible importance.

clue.text: Wrongly take unorthodox measures, driving out troops

indicators.note: unorthodox means irregular, so the letters that remain are shuffled
driving out means expelling, so the troops' letters leave the word measures

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps

explanation.surface: Someone takes unusual steps to remove soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving out' removes RE (Royal Engineers) from MEASURES, leaving MEASUS, which 'unorthodox' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp or seize without right, as one may unlawfully take on power.

clue.text: Drunken dame in boat couldn't stand

indicators.note: drunken means reeling, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman on a boat is unable to stay upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couldn't stand' looks like her being unable to stay upright; it means detested.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to be unable to tolerate it.

clue.text: Note girl has broken free of the bourgeoisie

indicators.note: the girl escapes from the social group, so her letters are removed from it

parts.note: the bourgeoisie is the middle class
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman writes a letter announcing she has escaped her comfortable suburban origins.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Note' looks like a letter she writes; it is a musical note. LASS is removed from MIDDLE CLASS, leaving MIDDLE C.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the musical tone nearest the centre of a piano keyboard.

clue.text: Aggressive-sounding manner

indicators.note: sounding means the word is heard spoken, giving a word that is said the same way

parts.note: mean can mean vicious or aggressive, as a mean dog

explanation.surface: A demeanour that comes across as hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAN, as in a mean dog, is said the same way as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or air, their outward demeanour.

clue.text: Young swimmer gets soaking when crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the soaking word spans the lake letter

parts.note: a ducking is a soaking, a plunge into water
L is a standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A child gets drenched swimming across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young swimmer' suggests a child; it is a baby duck. L goes inside DUCKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby duck is a juvenile waterbird that paddles.

clue.text: Loire regularly offers habitat for animal or bird

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of Loire is taken

explanation.surface: The Loire valley provides homes for wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: In hunting usage the lie is the place where an animal or game bird rests.
explanation.definitionFit: In field sports the spot where a creature lies hidden or rests is its lair.

clue.text: Fancy Tory taking parliamentary constituency, you say

indicators.note: you say means spoken out loud, so the words are matched by their sound

parts.note: a Tory is a Con, a Conservative, and a constituency is a seat in Parliament

explanation.surface: A Conservative wins a seat in Parliament, so to speak, in some fanciful way.
explanation.walkthrough: CON (Conservative) + SEAT is spoken like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceit is a fanciful notion or elaborate figure of speech, a whim.

clue.text: Gershwin, say, composed air

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these three letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The songwriter Gershwin wrote a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue lacks its letter count. 'Composed' fits the musical surface but signals rearranging AIR. Ira Gershwin wrote lyrics for his brother George's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira was the lyricist brother of George Gershwin, so this forename is an example of a Gershwin.

clue.text: Diversion in London cinema

parts.note: the Smoke is an old nickname for London
a screen is a cinema auditorium, as in a multiplex's screens

explanation.surface: A distraction occurs inside a picture house in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is a long-standing British nickname for London, from its coal-fire fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloud laid down to hide movements, and by extension anything meant to divert attention.

clue.text: She won't work till the cows come home

definitions.text: She won't work till the cows come home

parts.words: She won't work till the cows come home
parts.note: the idiom means she will never work, but literally her day's work starts when the herd returns to be milked

explanation.surface: A lazy woman will never get round to working.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid's task is drawing milk from the herd, which begins once the animals return from pasture.

clue.text: Do get away from church

parts.note: to flee is to get away
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to escape from the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a helping verb but is the definition: to do someone is to swindle them.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang to do someone is to cheat them, and to strip someone of money by trickery is the same.

clue.text: East's still cold

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East
still means not moving

explanation.surface: The eastern region is still freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East's' reads as East is: E followed by a word for still.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold in manner means unfeeling, showing no passion.

clue.text: During escape securely fasten torch

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the fastening word goes within the escape word

parts.note: flight is escape, as in taking flight
to lash is to tie down securely

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing remembers to tie the torch down tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torch' is the British word for a portable battery lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a torch is the hand-held battery lamp Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Indian yoghurt I obtained is on the turn

indicators.note: on the turn means turning round, so the words I and obtained are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: had means got or obtained

explanation.surface: Some yoghurt from India that someone bought is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' suggests milk souring, but it reverses I HAD, giving DAHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahi is the curd or yoghurt of South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Row leaving parade ground

definitions.meaning: soldiers dismissed from a parade break ranks and depart

explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel severs a friendship, and troops told to dismiss break ranks and leave the square.

clue.text: Joins the cast in disarray after start of act

indicators.note: after places the jumbled letters behind the opening letter
the start of the word act is its opening letter
in disarray means in confusion, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Actors fall into confusion after the first act begins.
explanation.walkthrough: THE CAST rearranged ('in disarray') follows A, the start of 'act'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach things is to fasten or link them together.

clue.text: Believer — female, presumably — outwardly rather wet

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the damp word encloses the other piece

parts.note: moist means damp, rather wet
a female is presumably not he, a male

explanation.surface: A woman of faith is described as somewhat damp on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female, presumably' is NOT HE, set inside MOIST, which is what 'outwardly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that there is a single god is a kind of religious believer.

clue.text: With German supporting Democrat, I got into bed with fascist leader

definitions.text: I got into bed with fascist leader

parts.note: mit is German for with
for means in favour of, supporting

explanation.surface: A woman confesses to an affair with a fascist chief, with German and Democrat help.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Mitford married Sir Oswald Mosley, leader of the British Union of Fascists.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, one of the famous aristocratic sisters, wed the British fascist chief Oswald Mosley.

clue.text: Non-standard pronunciation one's detected in old recording

indicators.note: something detected in a record is found inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record, an old format
one is I and 's is is, giving I S

explanation.surface: A speech defect can be heard on a vintage disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', I + S, placed inside LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment in which s sounds come out as th is an irregular way of speaking.

clue.text: As writer, show nepotism?

definitions.meaning: to promote one's relatives, to advance one's family

explanation.surface: A novelist is accused of favouring relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Pushkin was the great Russian poet; read as two words, the name means to push forward one's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pushkin was a Russian author, and favouring relatives means advancing family members.

clue.text: Black eye given by 14?

definitions.meaning: a bruised eye after a punch
a thing that shines, as a torch does

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a bruised eye, and literally something emitting light, as a torch does.

clue.text: Old Egyptian sailor coming back in at that moment

indicators.note: in places the turned sailor inside the time word

parts.note: then means at that time

indicators.note: coming back signals that the sailor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor returns home just at the right moment in an ancient tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back' turns the sailor round. Thebes was a city of ancient Egypt, so 'Old Egyptian' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a capital of ancient Egypt, so an inhabitant was an ancient Egyptian.

clue.text: Experts offer moral support, initially rejected

indicators.note: the opening letter of the phrase is turned away, so it is dropped

parts.note: to hold hands with someone is to support and comfort them

explanation.surface: Seasoned professionals offer encouragement, but it is turned down at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially rejected' drops the first letter, H, of HOLD HANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans with long experience in a field are skilled practitioners.

clue.text: After little time, be triumphant in match

indicators.note: after places the word for winning behind the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to win is to be triumphant

explanation.surface: After a short while, a player wins the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a game to be won; it means an exact counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something identical to another is its double or counterpart.

clue.text: Wild West pioneers at journey's end were no longer dry

definitions.text: Wild West pioneers at journey's end were
definitions.meaning: settlers who had travelled west by covered cart got down from it on arrival
a former teetotaller who has started drinking again

explanation.definitionFit: Literally having climbed down from the covered cart, and idiomatically back on the booze after abstaining.

clue.text: Female departs, after a fashion

indicators.note: after puts the departure letter behind the a

parts.note: D stands for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: A woman leaves, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a fashion' looks like a set phrase; it splits, with 'fashion' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a short-lived fashion.

clue.text: Meekly suppresses fearful cry

indicators.note: suppresses means holds within, so the word Meekly keeps the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A timid person stifles a scream of fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a timid person stifling a scream; 'suppresses' signals letters held within 'Meekly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic exclamation of alarm or fright.

clue.text: Writer having no energy avoids working

indicators.note: having no means lacking, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: dodges means avoids
E is the symbol for energy
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: An author with no energy avoids getting down to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no energy' takes E from DODGES. Charles Dodgson wrote as Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lutwidge Dodgson was the real name of Lewis Carroll, the author of the Alice books.

clue.text: Retires, having stored money in pots? The opposite

indicators.note: the opposite of money stored in pots is pots stored in money, so the pots go inside

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
urns are pots or vases

explanation.surface: Someone goes to bed after hiding their cash in jars.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'having stored money in pots' puts the cash in the jars; 'The opposite' swaps the roles, so the pots go inside the money.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to bed for the night is to retire.
